title: SDK Release + Migration Checklist (Auth/Retry/Timeout/Streaming Parity)
content:
Purpose
This is the release + migration checklist for SDK behavior standardization work (auth, retries, timeouts, streaming). Primary goal is to ship parity across Python/TypeScript/Go with clear semver decisions, customer-safe rollouts, and a repeatable backout plan.

Applies to
- Hosted API SDKs: python / typescript / go
- Changes to: auth config + header rules, retry + backoff defaults, timeout defaults, streaming semantics, error taxonomy
- Docs + quickstarts + examples aligned to new standards
- Conformance test harness gating releases

Owners / roles (for sign-offs)
- Release coordinator: Connor O’Brien
- Tech lead (standards): Ibrahim Khan
- SDK leads: Dana Lo (TS), Mateusz Zielinski (Go), (Python lead via DevEx rotation)
- Docs: Elliot Price / Wei Chen
- SRE reviewer: Rafael Mendes (retry safety)
- Security reviewer: Marcus Lin (auth handling, redaction)
- Support contact: Dev Patel (ticket correlation, comms readiness)


0) Release intent + scope lock (T-7 to T-3 days)
[ ] Confirm which repos/packages are releasing (python, ts, go, docs, quickstarts, examples)
[ ] List the exact behavior changes (customer-visible deltas). Keep this as bullet points in the release PR description and the changelog.
[ ] Confirm conformance test suite version and scenarios included (don’t expand test scope on release day).
[ ] Confirm whether any changes are behind config flags, and whether defaults are changing.
[ ] Confirm required platform/gateway dependencies (e.g., Retry-After/request-id header guarantees) are already deployed.

Notes
- If we are changing DEFAULTS (e.g., retries enabled by default where previously off), treat as higher risk even if API surface is unchanged.


1) Semver decision checklist (must be explicit in PR + release notes)
Goal: choose the smallest safe version bump consistent with semver, but do not under-bump behavior changes that break common integrations.

1A. Patch release is allowed if ALL are true
[ ] No new required configuration
[ ] No breaking changes to public types/signatures
[ ] Behavior changes are strictly bug-fixes that align with documented behavior OR with “reasonable expectation” (e.g., redacting secrets in logs)
[ ] Retry/timeout/streaming changes only reduce failures without changing success semantics (no new automatic retries on non-idempotent operations)
[ ] Backward compatibility maintained for env vars/config keys (aliases kept)

1B. Minor release is typical when ANY are true
[ ] New configuration options added (non-breaking)
[ ] Default behavior changes that may be observed but are expected to be safe (e.g., more consistent error types/messages; default timeouts adjusted)
[ ] New telemetry hooks or new structured error fields
[ ] Deprecations introduced (but old behavior still supported)

1C. Major release required when ANY are true
[ ] Default behavior change that can break production flows (examples: new automatic retries that can cause duplicate side effects; streaming cancellation semantics change; required header changes)
[ ] Removal/rename of public APIs or config keys (including env var name removal)
[ ] Error class/type hierarchy changes that break existing catch/instanceof logic (common in TS/Go)
[ ] Auth sourcing order changes that can select a different key than before in typical env setups (multi-tenant/server contexts)

Decision log (fill this out per SDK)
- Python: version bump = ____ (patch/minor/major), rationale: ____
- TypeScript: version bump = ____ (patch/minor/major), rationale: ____
- Go: version bump = ____ (patch/minor/major), rationale: ____


2) Changelog + release notes language (customer-facing)
Checklist
[ ] Add “Behavior change” bullets separate from “Fixes” and “New”
[ ] Call out default retry policy: which status codes, max attempts, and budget (high-level; details link to docs)
[ ] Call out timeout defaults separately for streaming vs non-streaming
[ ] Call out streaming disconnect behavior (what is surfaced vs retried, and what is never retried)
[ ] Call out auth changes: env var names, header used, config precedence, and redaction
[ ] Provide “How to opt out / tune” section (per SDK config snippets)
[ ] Add a “Potential impact” bullet written in plain language (e.g., “You may see fewer 429 retry storms; you may see faster failures when total timeout is exceeded.”)
[ ] Include “Request ID” mention: where to find it and how to pass it to Support

Changelog wording do/don’t
- DO: “Retries now respect Retry-After and apply exponential backoff with jitter; max retry time is bounded by a retry budget.”
- DO: “Streaming disconnects are surfaced as a StreamingDisconnectedError; SDK does not auto-resume the stream.”
- DON’T: “Improved reliability” without specifying what changed.
- DON’T: “Fixed timeouts” (ambiguous). Specify connect/read/overall.


3) Migration guide checklist (docs + repo RELEASE.md / MIGRATING.md)
Required sections
[ ] Summary: what changed + why (tie to parity + reliability)
[ ] Who is impacted (identify likely breakage patterns)
[ ] Before/after code snippets for Python/TS/Go
[ ] Auth migration
    [ ] Env var names and precedence order
    [ ] How to set per-request key in multi-tenant apps
    [ ] Logging/exception redaction expectations (what is masked)
[ ] Retry migration
    [ ] New defaults (attempts, backoff, jitter, budget)
    [ ] How to disable retries
    [ ] How to set per-request overrides
    [ ] How to detect retry exhaustion (error type + fields)
    [ ] Guidance on idempotency: when NOT to enable retries
[ ] Timeout migration
    [ ] Default values for streaming vs non-streaming
    [ ] Distinguish: connect timeout vs overall timeout vs read timeout
    [ ] Mapping of timeout errors (name + how to catch)
[ ] Streaming migration
    [ ] Cancellation semantics (Ctrl-C, AbortController, context cancel)
    [ ] How mid-stream disconnects surface
    [ ] Safe retry guidance (usually: do not auto-retry streams; restart request only if your app can tolerate duplicate tokens/side effects)
[ ] Troubleshooting section
    [ ] “Hangs on streaming” / proxy buffering notes
    [ ] “429s + throttling got worse” (how to tune retry budget)
    [ ] “Timeout vs cancel confusion” (Go context)
[ ] Rollout notes (if staged): which versions contain the change and any flags

Docs wiring
[ ] Docs page updated (canonical guidance)
[ ] Quickstarts updated (copy/paste safe)
[ ] Examples updated (show best practices)
[ ] Ensure consistent terminology across languages (same names for concepts even if types differ)


4) Pre-release quality gates (must be green for each SDK)
Conformance + CI
[ ] Conformance test harness passing in CI for the release candidate commit
[ ] No ignored/flaky tests added in the release window (exceptions require Sahana approval + issue filed)
[ ] Run conformance against mocked gateway scenarios:
    [ ] 429 burst with Retry-After
    [ ] 503 flap
    [ ] Connection reset mid-request
    [ ] Partial SSE frames
    [ ] Context/Abort cancellation mid-stream

Behavioral checks (quick manual sanity)
[ ] Auth: missing key error message includes remediation and does NOT print secrets
[ ] Auth: invalid key error does not leak full header value
[ ] Retries: verify no “retry storm” on persistent 429 (budget caps)
[ ] Retries: ensure request-id is logged/returned in error when available
[ ] Timeouts: confirm overall timeout triggers in realistic time (not infinite read)
[ ] Streaming: confirm cancellation closes sockets promptly (no process hang)

Security / compliance
[ ] Security sign-off for auth handling + redaction (Marcus)
[ ] Confirm debug logging defaults are safe (no secrets) and opt-in


5) Release execution steps (day-of)
Per SDK
[ ] Freeze: merge window agreed with SDK leads (no last-minute refactors)
[ ] Tag/Version bump PR merged with changelog + migration guide link
[ ] Publish package:
    - Python: PyPI publish + verify install from clean env
    - TypeScript: npm publish + verify install + types
    - Go: tag + module version available (proxy)
[ ] Publish docs/quickstarts/examples PRs (or ensure already merged) and verify live site updated
[ ] Post-release smoke test using released artifacts (not local build)

Comms
[ ] Post internal Slack note in #devex and #support with:
    - versions released
    - key behavior changes
    - troubleshooting pointers
    - links to migration guide
    - how to capture request-id + logs safely
[ ] If major/breaking: email to affected enterprise customers (via PM/CS plan)


6) Rollout monitoring (T+0 to T+72 hours)
Dashboards / signals to watch
[ ] Support volume: new tickets tagged sdk-retry, sdk-streaming, sdk-auth
[ ] 429 rate and retry amplification (client-side): look for increased request counts per user action
[ ] Error mix changes: TimeoutError, RetryExhausted, StreamingDisconnected
[ ] Median + tail latency (p95/p99) for typical SDK operations if client telemetry exists
[ ] Connection churn / socket errors (streaming)
[ ] Customer-reported symptoms:
    - “stuck/hanging stream”
    - “throttling got worse”
    - “auth broke in CI/prod”

Monitoring checklist
[ ] Identify top 5 request-ids with failures and validate error fields are present
[ ] Spot-check that Retry-After is being honored (where present)
[ ] Confirm no regressions in cancellation behavior (esp. TS AbortController)

Decision points
[ ] If we see sustained retry amplification or extended throttling loops: prepare patch release with safer defaults (reduce attempts/budget, stronger respect for Retry-After)
[ ] If streaming disconnect errors spike: confirm gateway/proxy behavior and consider updating docs + setting a safer default read timeout


7) Backout plan (must be written before release)
Principle: we prefer a fast follow patch release over yanking when possible, but we should be ready to yank if the breakage is severe.

Backout triggers (examples)
[ ] Auth regression preventing clients from authenticating with standard env setups
[ ] Retry storm behavior causing customer rate limit lockout / cascading failures
[ ] Streaming change causing hangs/leaks in common runtimes

Backout options
A) Fast follow patch (preferred when feasible)
[ ] Revert default change / reduce aggressiveness
[ ] Preserve new config options but change defaults
[ ] Ship within 24 hours with clear notes (“rollback of default behavior; flags remain available”)

B) Yank / deprecate release (use when severe and widespread)
Python (PyPI)
[ ] Yank the offending version (leave metadata + message)
[ ] Publish a known-good patch/minor immediately
TypeScript (npm)
[ ] Deprecate version with message pointing to fixed version
[ ] Publish patched version; update dist-tag if using (e.g., latest)
Go
[ ] Use retract directive in go.mod (if applicable) and publish a new tag
[ ] Document workaround (pin prior version)

C) Docs hotfix
[ ] If behavior is correct but docs misled users: ship docs fix immediately + update troubleshooting

Operational checklist for backout
[ ] Open incident-like Slack thread with DevEx + SRE + Support
[ ] Post customer-facing advisory (status page only if warranted; otherwise docs + support macro)
[ ] Add “what happened / prevention” note to the project retrospective


8) Post-release follow-ups (T+1 week)
[ ] Retro: what surprised us; update conformance tests to cover the gap
[ ] Update this checklist if any step was missing
[ ] Close the loop on top tickets (SUP-9321/9334/9342/9355) with final resolution notes and affected versions
[ ] Confirm parity matrix updated to reflect shipped behavior (v2 post-review)

Appendix: Release artifacts to attach to the release issue
- Version numbers (py/ts/go)
- Links to changelogs
- Link to migration guide
- Conformance test run link (CI)
- Known issues + workarounds
- Monitoring summary at T+72h (brief)
